research_run_caveat: This run executed 16 successful WebSearch queries before the session-wide search budget (200/200, shared across agents) was exhausted. Every WebFetch attempt (40+ URLs across army.mil, dvidshub.net, gao.gov, sam.gov, comptroller.war.gov, sbir.gov, diu.mil, usaspending.gov, congress.gov, defensescoop.com, breakingdefense.com, executivegov.com, lockheedmartin.com, anduril.com, palantir.com, wikipedia.org and others) was blocked by the network egress proxy, and the Bigdata.com news connector returned out-of-credits. All facts below therefore come from search-result snippets and titles, not from full-document reads. Fields marked 'Public evidence insufficient' were not retrievable in this run and must not be treated as absent in reality. Recommend a re-run with fetch access before investment-grade use.

organizations.current_status_2026: FACT: PEO C3T redesignated PEO C3N on 2024-10-09 after absorbing PEO EIS network portfolios in the Oct-2023 'PEO Optimization' (army.mil/article/280427; defensescoop 2024-10-09). FACT: PEO C3N restructured into 'Capability Program Executive Command, Control, Communications, and Network (CPE C3N)' in a Dec-2025 'major reorganization' tied to NGC2 (army.mil/article/289377; Army DCS G-6 X post). FACT (MEDIUM): by Feb-2026 the organization is styled 'Capability Program Executive Command and Control Information Network (CPE C2IN)' (BG Taylor bio PDF dated Feb 2026 on api.army.mil; DVIDS unit page CPEC2IN; peoc3n.army.mil/Careers/About-CPE-C2IN). INFERENCE: the C3N->C2IN rename occurred between Dec-2025 and Feb-2026; exact effective date not retrieved. Reorganized sub-offices confirmed by snippet: 'PM C2 Infrastructure' (Col. Stuart McMillan, DPM Jonathan D'Aprile) and 'PL C2 Enablers' (Douglas Burbey, deputy Lisa Bell; interoperability enablers, 24/7/365 support). NOT VERIFIED in this run: whether 'PM C2 Applications', 'PM C2 Data/AI', 'PM C2 Transport', 'PM Tactical Radios', 'PM Tactical Network', 'PM Mission Command' exist under those names after the reorg. PM Interoperability, Integration and Services (PM I2S, stood up 2020; Matthew Maier PM from 2021-01-29) was still issuing an INB2 solicitation under 'PEO C3N' branding; its post-reorg status is unverified.

organizations.startup_relevance: HIGH. This is the program office that awarded both NGC2 prototype OTAs and that owns the four NGC2 layers (applications, data, infrastructure, transport) into which the Army is consolidating C2 funding lines. Practical entry for a two-founder startup is as a team member/subcontractor to an NGC2 team lead (Anduril or Lockheed) or via xTech/SBIR topics sponsored by CPE C2IN, not as a prime on a $26M-$100M OTA.

programs.name: Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2)
programs.owner: CPE C2IN (formerly PEO C3N) as acquirer; requirement side formerly Army Futures Command / C2 CFT, now T2COM (INFERENCE)
programs.description: Mobile, four-layer C2 architecture (applications, data, infrastructure, transport) built on a common/integrated data layer with government-approved, non-proprietary APIs between layers, intended to give commanders faster decisions and replace legacy mission command systems. Reported to have become an official program of record in 2025 (National Defense, 2025-04-22; acquisition pathway not verified).
programs.status_2026: FACT: PC-C5 (March 2025, NTC) 'proof of principle' -> prototype OTAs to Team Anduril (4ID, July 2025) and Team Lockheed Martin (25ID, Sept 2025) -> division-scale exercises (Ivy Mass; Lightning Surge 1 Jan 2026) -> PC-C6 (July 2026, NTC) planned as division-scale force-on-force NGC2 validation and likely start of fielding decisions. FACT: Army intends to field NGC2 to all 11 divisions over five years at 2-3 divisions/year (Breaking Defense 2026-05). FACT: Congress capped FY2026 NGC2 funding with conditions (Federal News Network 2026-02; details not retrieved). FACT: GAO-26-108019 (2026) found the Army needs better schedule and cost information to support scaling the battlefield network (title only retrieved). PC-C6 outcomes and any post-PC-C6 production/scaling awards: Public evidence insufficient in this run.
vendors: Lockheed Martin Rotary and Mission Systems (team lead, 25ID) with unnamed 'non-traditional' partners

programs.third_party_software_openness: FACT (from Army/vendor statements, not independent test): NGC2's data integration layer is meant to allow rapid buildout of apps across warfighting functions (fires, intel, logistics, protection) and a common COP; layers interface via 'Government approved, non-proprietary APIs'; the Army says it wants on-ramps/off-ramps to onboard or offboard vendors and capabilities based on performance, and told industry to 'bring your core strength' (army.mil/article/290431). Team Anduril members and later joiners (e.g., Rune Technologies for logistics) show third-party apps entering via the team lead. Caveat: the actual API specifications and whether an independent startup can integrate without the team lead's sponsorship are not publicly documented in retrieved material - INFERENCE, MEDIUM confidence.

procurement_pathways.how_it_works_here: Army prize competitions (xTechSearch, xTechPacific, xTechOverwatch, xTechIgnite, AI Grand Challenge, etc.) run by the Army SBIR|STTR / FUZE office: white paper -> pitch -> demo at Army events (e.g., HMI Summit Oct 2025 for xTechOverwatch); winners get cash, an accelerator, and an invitation to submit an Army SBIR Phase I or Direct-to-Phase-II proposal.
procurement_pathways.typical_award_size: $15K participation prizes up to ~$500K per winner; xTechOverwatch pool up to $1M; xTechPacific paid $450K in prizes plus 'millions in follow-on contracts'.
procurement_pathways.timeline: Competition cycles of roughly 3-6 months; follow-on SBIR adds 3-6+ months (INFERENCE).

recent_examples.what: Cash prizes and follow-on SBIR contracts

procurement_pathways.fit_for_two_founder_startup: HIGH - designed for exactly this profile; low cost of entry, soldier feedback, and a bridge to SBIR money.
procurement_pathways.eligibility_notes: Most xTech competitions are limited to 'eligible small businesses' and follow-on SBIR requires SBIR eligibility (small, for-profit, >50% owned by U.S. citizens or permanent residents or by other eligible entities). With one founder not a U.S. person, cap-table structure needs specialist review; the German founder counts toward the U.S.-ownership test only once a permanent resident (INFERENCE from the SBIR Policy Directive; verify). Some xTech tracks (xTechInternational) are open to foreign firms.

procurement_pathways.how_it_works_here: Army FUZE SBIR|STTR: after the 2026 reauthorization, the Army posted five funding opportunities; Army SBIR uses open topics and Direct-to-Phase-II; program reportedly shifting to portfolio-level ('the whole vs. the parts') management (FNN 2026-05). ARL/DEVCOM also issue SBIR/STTR topics.
procurement_pathways.typical_award_size: Phase I ~$100K-$250K; Phase II / D2P2 ~$1M-$2M+ (INFERENCE from Army SBIR norms; specific 2026 caps not retrieved).
procurement_pathways.timeline: Topic open ~30-60 days; award 3-6 months after close (INFERENCE).

procurement_pathways.fit_for_two_founder_startup: HIGH if eligible; the main non-dilutive path to a first Army contract.

Similarly, TITAN production creates a Palantir/Anduril subcontract ecosystem.

procurement_pathways.timeline: Weeks to months, driven by the prime's integration sprints and exercise calendar (Ivy Sting/Ivy Mass, Lightning Surge, PC-C6).

how_a_startup_gets_in: Sequenced, based on retrieved evidence: (1) Pick one NGC2 layer problem the Army has named - a warfighting-function app (fires, intel, logistics, protection) on the data layer, or a NetOps/DDIL tool for S6s - and build against open standards so it can sit on a common data layer. (2) Enter an Army xTech competition (xTechSearch for general, xTechPacific for INDOPACOM 'tyranny of distance', xTechOverwatch for autonomy/sensor networks) to get cash, soldier feedback and the SBIR Phase I / Direct-to-Phase-II invitation; resolve SBIR ownership eligibility with counsel first given one non-U.S.-person founder. (3) In parallel, approach the NGC2 team leads - Anduril (4th ID; members incl. Palantir, Microsoft, Govini, Striveworks, ICE, RII; Rune Technologies joined later) and Lockheed Martin (25th ID data layer) - to be onboarded as a team member for Ivy Sting/Ivy Mass or Lightning Surge events; this is the only demonstrated route by which small software firms have entered NGC2 to date. (4) Engage the Army Applications Laboratory and CPE C2IN/CPE ISW industry engagements at Aberdeen Proving Ground (technical exchange meeting schedule not verified this run) and watch sam.gov NGC2 notices (an NGC2 notice and an updated presolicitation exist but could not be read). (5) Target Project Convergence Capstone events (PC-C6 July 2026; next cycle 2027) via a team lead or T2COM RFI, since those are where fielding decisions are informed. (6) For ISR/PED products, pursue CPE ISW's HYDRA API and the Palantir TITAN ecosystem now that TITAN is in production. Caution: Congress capped FY2026 NGC2 funds and GAO flagged cost/schedule gaps, so scaling beyond two divisions is not yet contractually evidenced.
